claim: A gateway-side exporter that shows CRC errors and bridge outages the network server never sees.
data_label: simulated data: replayed traffic, no real gateway
limit: Never run on real gateway hardware; Yocto recipe unbuilt, no real ARM CPU figures.
alt: Dark panel titled What the gateway itself sees: three stat tiles (57 uplinks per minute, 5.7 percent CRC error ratio, 36 percent TX duty versus limit) above a line chart of a simulated CRC-error burst peaking near 36 percent.
post:
A LoRaWAN gateway can look healthy from the network server and still be quietly sick: CRC-failed packets never leave the box, a backhaul bridge can drop and recover, and downlink rejections stay local.

I wrote a small open-source Rust exporter that runs on the gateway itself. It sits between the Semtech UDP packet forwarder and its bridge, relays every datagram byte for byte, and turns a copy into Prometheus metrics: uplinks per channel and spreading factor, CRC-error ratio, RSSI and SNR histograms, airtime and duty-cycle estimates, and host health. A Grafana dashboard and a docker compose demo are included.

Measured numbers: the stripped armv7 hard-float glibc binary is 515 KiB, the fully static one 579 KiB, and 78 tests pass in CI, including qemu smoke runs of both ARM builds. In the demo, a replayed 40-device fleet shows an injected CRC-error burst peaking around 36 percent.

What is not verified: it has never run on real gateway hardware. All traffic is simulated or hand-written fixtures from the protocol spec, the Yocto recipe was never built with BitBake, and I have no real ARM CPU or memory figures.

If you operate gateways, which gateway-side signal do you wish you could see without logging in over SSH?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/lorawan-gateway-health
